topics.topic: Whether a project-create replay after request-id removal guarantees creation or undergoes current create checks
questions: When the former request id makes the call a new create but its submitted facts now fail an ordinary create check, is it refused or must it make and answer a new record?

After anonymisation removes the request id, must the resubmitted project create always make a new project, or is it an ordinary new create that can be refused because its formerly valid customer is now ineligible?

Does reuse of a removed request id guarantee creation despite conditions that changed since the original create, or does it merely make the request a fresh create that may be refused by all current checks?

quotes:
A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
a customer reference that is unknown, erased, restricted or ended refused (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57);
judgement.why: The first passage guarantees that the fresh create makes and answers a new record, while the second refuses that same fresh create when its customer has become ineligible.

bases.passage:
A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure
   removes (M01, M04); a create arriving after that with the same request id
   is a new create, answered with the new record it made, so it is not silent
   (R0-36, owner, 2026-11-01).
bases.rests_on:
This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values (owner,
2026-11-01). Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything
that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new
create, and its answer shows the new record it made.

witness.initial: Customer C is eligible, and project P naming C exists after the owner created it with request id K.
events: The owner archives project P after confirming.
The owner erases archived project P after confirming and chooses anonymisation, which removes its request id and customer link.
The owner resubmits P's original create request with request id K and customer reference C.
outcomes: The removed request id makes the request a new create that creates and answers a new project.
The current refusal condition for a restricted customer refuses the request and creates no project.
witness.observer: The owner sees a new project or a refusal, and the catalogue and audit log differ.

topics.topic: Whether an identical replacement upload invalidates an existing import confirmation and how replacement is identified
questions: How does Registry distinguish replacement by an identical upload so that the old confirmation is refused: must every accepted upload invalidate the pending confirmation, or may the old confirmation remain valid when the digest and all bound inputs are unchanged?

When the owner re-uploads byte-for-byte identical content after the import confirmation step was shown, is the existing confirmation still valid, and what recorded fact distinguishes the replacement from the original upload?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P1: the added concurrency-review wording does not change the unchanged rules that an identical re-upload replaces the file and invalidates the earlier confirmation.

precedent.topic: Identity or generation mechanism that invalidates an import confirmation after re-upload
quotes:
The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, in the
   process's memory only — never in the store, never on a disk — until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session — one of the same bytes included — or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept — also when the new file has
   the same bytes.
precedent.why: The texts expressly treat every later upload, identical bytes included, as replacing the earlier file and require the earlier confirmation to be refused; the internal mechanism used to enforce that outcome does not change observable behaviour.
